A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLMEVALDB research, with readable main text, tables, figures, and appendices A–F. Textual and visual inspection supports reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: V2 reports an original human evaluation of 40 extracted records in Section 3.1 and original analyses of prompting behavior in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains the original extraction-quality evaluation and analyses of LLMEVALDB, including human evaluation results and comparisons across prompting configurations.

M1.justification: The extraction, augmentation, and two-stage description-generation pipeline remains unchanged. Section 2.4 and Appendix A clarify that refusal when uncertain triggers source-paper extraction; they do not establish a newly introduced procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 18,127 records from 1,737 papers, four target models, and task categories. Dataset examples and coverage in Appendices D–E are unchanged.

E2.justification: CoT and standard/direct prompting remain the comparison methods, and the comparison with Sprague et al.'s manual analysis is retained. New citations do not introduce evaluated baselines; the removed demonstration-count contrast concerns configurations of existing methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.4's reported comparison design is narrowed by dropping the more-shot versus less-shot CoT contrast, including its filtered-paper counterpart. Retained comparisons use unchanged settings; no rerun or change to their samples, metrics, or controls is established.

E4.justification: Tables 5 and 8 remove the CoT-specific demonstration-count sensitivity analysis and its peer-reviewed-subset check. The broader ICL more-shot versus less-shot analysis in Figure 9, negative-case analysis, and remaining peer-reviewed comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: The quartile reporting, one-sided bootstrap procedure, and Bonferroni threshold remain unchanged. No new runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or testing procedures are disclosed. Section 4.4's added significance wording is an outcome claim without an accompanying new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: V3 removes the more-shot versus less-shot CoT results: median/Q1/Q3 of 3.1/0.4/9.0 for all papers and 5.0/2.3/10.7 for filtered papers. Retained numerical results are unchanged. Section 4.4 newly calls the retained +3.0-point few-shot CoT gain significant.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. The empirical performance-difference definitions remain equivalent; revised delta notation in the tables does not change mathematical content.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the claim that deriving new performance insights through this approach is 'a first in the field.' The principal dataset, efficiency, replication, and prompting-behavior contributions remain unchanged in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 replaces its CoT-specific inference that demonstration presence matters more than quantity with an emphasis that demonstrations do not make CoT clearly outperform standard prompting. It also frames the within-CoT gain as replication of prior findings. Section 7's limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly makes explicit that the model was instructed to refuse answers when unsure about dataset information, explaining the existing fallback trigger. Other implementation settings, extraction prompts, resource estimates, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Bai et al. (2022), Constitutional AI, and Zhang et al. (2022b), Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting. Section 4.4 explicitly connects its finding to Wei et al. and Zhang et al., while the introduction narrows its novelty wording. Overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: Section 4.4 is rewritten into two numbered questions and corresponding analyses. Limited wording edits also occur in the introduction, description-generation explanation, related work, and Appendix A. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Tables 5 and 8 are shortened and relabeled; Tables 6 and 9 receive revised headings, captions, signs, and row ordering. These changes cause local reflow. All nine figures remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 makes Section 4.4 easier to assess by separating within-CoT demonstration effects from CoT-versus-standard comparisons and removing its quantity-versus-presence inference. Appendix A also clarifies the fallback trigger. These provide modest clarity and reproducibility gains, although removing CoT sensitivity results reduces detail and the new 'significant' claim lacks a corresponding reported test.
